claim: In 2021 the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation funded the biotechnology company Oxitec — based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, UK — to develop a genetically engineered 'self-limiting' Asian cattle tick (Rhipicephalus microplus), in which released males carry a gene that prevents their offspring reaching maturity, suppressing the population. Oxitec and the foundation describe the project as protecting cattle herds and global food security; the modified ticks have been studied only in UK labs and not released in the wild.

sources.label: Alliance for Science — 'Gates Foundation funds research to control cattle ticks through biotechnology' (May 2021)
sources.quote: The cattle tick is a devastating pest, causing high rates of cattle mortality, which in turn impacts the lives of farmers and food security globally.

sources.label: PolitiFact — 'No connection between Gates-funded modified ticks and alpha-gal syndrome' (Sep 1, 2023)
Kels Unfiltered / @unfilteredwithkels, Instagram reel DYkbLNVi8NG (May 20, 2026) — surfacing source

notes: Documented fact: the Gates Foundation funded Oxitec's genetically-engineered cattle-tick program (reported grants include $1.283M and a later $4.85M), targeting Rhipicephalus microplus; Oxitec is headquartered in Oxfordshire ('right in the backyard of Oxford University' in the reel). Oxitec CEO Grey Frandsen is quoted: 'The foundation's investment will enable us to expand our technology to improve the lives and livelihoods of communities around the world.' The reel's CEO 'Oxetech' is a whisper rendering of Oxitec. The reel's inference — that a project to protect livestock proves an intent to centralize control over who may produce meat — is insinuation, not in the record. R. microplus is a different species from the lone star tick that causes alpha-gal in humans, and Oxitec's design suppresses the tick population rather than spreading it; PolitiFact rated the engineered-tick/meat-allergy link false. Group C claims from the reel with no primary trace (NOT recorded): ticks dropped from low-flying planes onto farms, and an anonymous Ontario charter-pilot 'leak' about paid tick air-drops.
